subject: Mutual Plan: hypothesis verification & exit gates (MAP draft)
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Soto <alex.soto@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-04-12 09:15 PDT
Subject: Mutual plan draft + proposed verification tests

Alex — thanks again for the demo yesterday. As promised, attached is a compact MAP draft that focuses on 3 hypotheses we want to verify during the 4‑week evaluation and the concrete exit gates to move to pilot. High level: research > validate > commit.

Key asks from Acme (what we need from you):
- 2 production‑like workflows and a representative dataset slice (anonymized).
- 1 technical contact for KV cache and SSO test windows.
- Legal confirmation of data handling by week 2 (SOC2 scoping doc).

Our commitments (what Redwood will deliver):
- Baseline performance profile on your sample (p95 latency, tokens/sec).
- Acceptance test suite (see attached) including functional QA and smoke performance runs.
- Runbook for rollback and fallback to smaller model variant if perf < gate.

Proposed exit gates (pass all to go to pilot):
1) Latency: 95th percentile < 350ms for representative L1 workflows at 75th percentile load.
2) Quality: macro F1 on intent classification >= 0.92 on curated prompt set (see sheet).
3) Reliability: sustained error rate < 0.5% across 24h soak.
4) Security & compliance: evidence for data retention & logging enabled; legal signoff received.

Please review and flag anything you want changed — I can move the acceptance tests into a collaborative spreadsheet if you prefer to edit live.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555‑0184

Attachments: MAP-draft-v1.pdf, acceptance-tests-suite.xlsx
From: Alex Soto <alex.soto@acmehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-04-12 11:02 PDT
Subject: Re: Mutual plan draft + proposed verification tests

Thanks Stephanie — this looks practical and tight, appreciate the clarity. A couple quick notes from our side:

- We can provide two anonymized workflows by Monday (care coordination + intake triage).
- Legal needs a short summary of what logs look like (fields retained, retention window). Can Ben share the SOC2 evidence checklist?
- On quality: can we add a human‑review sampling requirement (10% of outputs during week 2) to validate edge cases?

If those items are agreeable I'll loop in Katie from HealthSphere (our platform owner) so she can schedule a 1‑hour environment setup window next week.

On the gates, the latency and reliability targets look reasonable. The F1 target is ambitious but acceptable for a first pass as long as we have the human review safety net.

—Alex
Alex Soto

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Soto <alex.soto@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-04-13 08:47 PDT
Subject: Re: Mutual plan draft + proposed verification tests

Alex, happy to take point on the SOC2 evidence checklist. I'll attach the standard evidence pack and a one‑page summary for legal (what fields, retention, where logs are stored, and access controls).

A couple of operational clarifications so we set realistic test windows:
- Environment: we'll spin up a dedicated inference pool for the eval (4 x A10 equivalent) but we should confirm expected concurrency so autoscaling thresholds are tuned.
- Performance tests: suggest two 30‑minute soak windows (week 1 and week 3) and a 6hr soak during week 4 for stability verification.
- Human review: we can enable a sampling hook to forward 10% of outputs to your reviewer queue; we'll provide a simple labeling UI for rapid feedback.

I'll drop the SOC2 pack and the performance runbook as attachments in the next email.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

Date: 2026-04-15 14:03 PDT
Subject: Re: Mutual plan draft + proposed verification tests — final MAP changes and next steps

Alex / Ben — summarized updates after our sync today and next steps to lock the MAP: 

Summary of changes we agreed to:
- Added human‑review sampling at 10% in week 2 and week 4 (safety net for edge cases).
- Legal checklist action: Ben to send SOC2 evidence pack and a 1‑page retention summary by EOD 4/15.
- Performance cadence: two 30‑minute soaks (wk1/wk3) + final 6‑hour endurance test (wk4).
- Acceptance tests updated: split into Functional (pass/fail) and Nonfunctional (quantitative gates).

Concrete next steps and owners (target dates):
- Acme: deliver anonymized workflows + sample data (owner: Alex) — due 2026‑04‑19.
- Redwood SE: SOC2 evidence + runbook (owner: Ben) — due 2026‑04‑15 (in progress).
- Redwood AE: finalize MAP and send link to collaborative sheet (owner: Stephanie) — due 2026‑04‑16.

Acceptance test highlights (short):
- Functional: end‑to‑end success rate >= 98% on scripted flows (no critical regressions).
- Latency: p95 < 350ms under expected concurrency (see runbook load profile).
- Quality: macro F1 >= 0.92 on curated set + human review pass rate >= 85% for sampled outputs.
- Reliability: error rate < 0.5% for a continuous 24h window during the 6h vs soak test expansion.

If there are no blockers I will: (1) publish the MAP to the shared doc; (2) move the acceptance-tests.xlsx to the shared folder and open edit rights for Alex and Katie; (3) set a calendar invite for the environment setup (45m) for next Wed.

Thanks everyone — feel free to reply with one‑line ACKs if this matches your view.

—Stephanie
